en: Therīgāthā 5.7 Pañcakanipāta Sakulātherīgāthā Sakulā, the Elder Nun I am Sakulā, daughter of a wealthy family, Born into a clan of great renown. Having heard the Dhamma from the Well-Gone One, I have gone forth into homelessness. For twenty-five years I have been one who has abandoned sensual pleasures; I am now eighty years of age. With a mind that is well-liberated, I dwell in the bliss of liberation. I am Sakulā, daughter of a wealthy family, Born into a clan of great renown. With a mind that is well-liberated
“While living here in the home,
having heard the Dhamma from a bhikkhu,
I saw the stainless Dhamma.”
Nirvana is the deathless state.
Having abandoned my son and daughter,
as well as wealth and grain;
Having had my hair shaved off,
I went forth into the homeless life;
being peaceful, I was a trainee.
Cultivating the straight path,
I abandoned lust and hatred,
as well as the taints associated with them.
Having received full ordination as a bhikkhunī,
I recollected my former births;
the divine eye was purified.
Pure and well-cultivated.
Having seen conditioned phenomena as alien,
born of causes, and subject to dissolution;
“I have abandoned all taints;
I have become cool and attained Nibbāna.
… Thus spoke the Elder Nun Sakulā.
